port_demand.core_behavioural_vm_per_cycle: reads: vx G x 32 b, vs 4*SW, vi SW, vq, vr, wqr 32 el, wxr 32 el, vh HS, vsl XSQ*XSW = 64 el, xs_vi SUN = 256, xs_rd 4*SUN = 1024 el, rom_x 64 el; writes: rom_we 128 scalar ports, xs_vm SUN = 256 el, xs_res SUN/8, vw_me G x 16, ww_q/h/x 32 el, xa/xb FLIT 16 el (ot_hdc_core_v41x.sv:196-325, ot_chip_v41x_tile.sv:551-625)
port_demand.finding: the core's SU alone reads 1,280 elements (80 rows) a cycle; the die buses carry 4 rows a cycle to the SU halves (contracts_hub G2). All die buses fully concurrent = 33 row ports; a 33-port crossbar over 32 banks at 512 b is not buildable in the slab. The memory subsystem built here has NP = 8 row ports (parameter); the VM sequencer must assign hub buses to ports per op (static schedule) and its cycle cost is a program-level number (next step)

rtl.ports: NP row ports {v, we, row[14], mask[16] element mask, d[512]}; reads return on the same port at fixed L = QD + 6 = 10 cycles, in order, never stall
rtl.semantics: exact behavioural-array order: ops take effect in (issue cycle, port) order; per-bank in-order queue, 1 op/bank/cycle on 1R1W macros; stall-free contract <= QD outstanding per bank else sticky fault (fail closed)
rtl.boundary: pin-registered requests (4 kept copies, <= 32 loads/bit), 2-flop reset sync, macro pins driven from the serve register, macro read data captured before any mux, outputs from flops, kept 128-b-slice select copies

bench.gold: PASS: NB32/QD4, NB8/QD4, NB8/QD2 x seeds 1-3 x 100k cycles (~0.47-0.56 M ops each, every read checked, 0 mismatches, max_occ = QD reached) + directed W->R/R->W same cycle, RAW chains, all ports busy, saturated bank, masked writes; +OVF floods a bank -> fault code 001 (PASS_OVF)

cycle_cost.note: every unit's VM read gains 9 cycles of pipeline fill (fixed latency, once per op pipeline, not per element); writes are posted (no latency visible to the issuer, RAW order preserved). QD = 2 gives L = 8 (+7) at a tighter per-bank burst bound. Bank-conflict cost: unit-stride row streams spread over 32 interleaved banks conflict-free; scattered element writes (capture) and gathers (vi) may exceed QD per bank -> the sequencer must pace them (program-level)
